title: Twachtman Exploring Different Styles
content: John Henry Twachtman(1853-1902) is best known for his atmospheric impressionism, where forms dissolve into a haze of small brushstrokes.The White Bridge, ca. 1895,Minneapolis Institute of ArtsBut he went through dramatically different styles before that. When he was studying at theAcadémie Julianin Paris, his paintings explored atonalistapproach. He uses soft grays and greens painted flat and a little out of focus.John Twachtman,“Springtime,”1884-1885, oil on canvas,36 7/8 x 50 in, Cincinnati Art MuseumBefore that, he explored the world more objectively.Here is a 24-year-oldJohn Henry Twachtmanpainting in a more realistic mode, with fine details and a full range of values. This grew out of a visitto Venice in 1878 in the company of Munich-trained Duveneck and Chase. Munich academic painters didn't hesitate to use extreme darks and blacks.One style isn't better than another, of course, but it's interesting to know that they were all produced by the same person. It's entirely natural for any of us to travel through completely different ways of seeing.--John Henry Twachtmanon Wikipedia
